title: A Dentist in a Digimon Adventure
section: Reflection after spending an academic year with R
text:
Reflection after spending an academic year with R
My encounter with applied statistics and coding was not intended for, rather it came spontaneously after a colleague of mine recommended taking the statistical methods course series. At first, I though it was way beyond my reach. Although mathematics and statistics were subjects I enjoyed, spending 7 years in the dental school was enough to lower my confidence in revisiting that field. My colleague, whom I am grateful for, made me reconsider my decision after saying “it is the most worthwhile subject you will get from this program”. Getting the best out of the MPH program was exactly what I wanted. That was when I realized that I wanted to challenge myself and go beyond my comfort zone.
The first obstacle I faced was not the concept of statistical methods, but the coding language. At first, it seemed impossible to understand the logic behind the coding system. So impossible to the point of regretting my decision. “Maybe this isn’t for me, why did do this to myself” I thought. However, as the classes progressed and after completing several assignments, the language started to seep in, and I began to intuitively understand its structure. Then, after completing multiple milestone (quizzes and projects) the language started to grow on me, so much that after completing the first course I started seeking more data sets to practice and play around with. I cannot deny the fact that I felt bitter with the way R was abruptly introduced to me, it felt as though I was thrown in it. But after some time, I realized that that may have been the best way to get started with it, otherwise I wouldn’t have mastered R this fast.
Although I was successfully earned an A in the first course, it did not ease my fears from the second course. After diving in the second course, I realized that coding became a lot smoother, while statistical concepts advanced and became harder. Still, it wasn’t as “impossible” as the first course was. Yes, it was a bewildering world to delve in, but over time, I started to feel home. “This may be something I can enjoy, something I can happily continue my studies with” were my thoughts.
I started this journey with a vague vision of my future. However, my adventure with R opened new pathways and opportunities unbeknownst to me, and most importantly, moved me closer to my goal; to make the world a better place for human dentition.

title: Salam!
text:

Salam!
I am Sarah Albalawi, a general dentist currently pursuing a master degree of public health (MPH) at Case Western Reserve University.
Ever since my undergraduate studies, I have always enjoyed dental public health projects and community services. I also had a knack for mathematics and, needless to say, the field of biostatistics intrigued me. During the dental internship program, I explored multiple specialties and disciplines of dentistry. While each carried a significant role in improving dental health, they were limited to the clinical setting and focused largely on treatment rather than prevention. Dental public health did not receive as much attention despite its imperative role in addressing root causes of oral diseases. My desire to join the preventive workforce and become a community dentist motivated me pursue the Master of Public Health degree.
